01

Essence

Tagline
Honouring tradition. Creating the future.
Vision
To teach the world that fine wine is alcohol optional.
Mission
To be recognised as the highest quality non-alcoholic wine maker in the world.
Position
The Dom Pérignon of non-alcoholic wine.Premium $30–50 for the current range; Luxury $50+ for the Reserve collection.
The line that matters
We don't make alcohol-free wine. We make exceptional wine that happens to be non-alcoholic.

Origin

BOLLE is the non-alcoholic wine for discerning wine lovers who believe exceptional taste does not have to depend on alcohol. Through a pioneering secondary fermentation process, lees ageing and provenance, we capture the purest expression of wine. Wines that excel in appearance, aroma, flavour and texture, exactly as they should.

What makes us different

  • Twice fermented. Unlike the rest of the category, BOLLE ferments a second time, including after dealcoholisation. This is the single most important thing to communicate.
  • Lees aged. Extended contact with the lees builds the texture and complexity that non-alcoholic wine is usually missing.
  • Provenance and IP. Grapes from distinguished regions, and a substantial body of intellectual property behind the process.
  • Product philosophy. Each bottle carries a narrative of passion, dedication and respect for nature, crafted by generations of expertise.
02

Values

5 values, each with its voice
ValueWhat it meansVoice
Inclusivity without compromise Everyone has the right to high quality wine, whether they drink alcohol or not. Never a lesser option; designed for drinkers and non-drinkers alike, so every guest feels part of the moment. "Everyone deserves something extraordinary in their glass."
Uncompromising quality We never settle. Premium ingredients, obsessive attention to taste, craft and credibility over shortcuts. At every touchpoint from product to packaging. "Created with purpose. Subtle craftsmanship in every pour."
Flavour-first innovation We lead with taste and push boundaries. R&D operates like a creative studio, not a production line. "We respect tradition, but we are not afraid to innovate."
Authenticity in every pour Honest about who we are and what we stand for. Open about ingredients, production and values. No gimmicks, no pretences. "Nothing extra. Everything essential."
Celebrate the choice Choosing not to drink should never feel like missing out. We uplift every choice with joy, not judgment, and support sober-friendly spaces and conversations. "Intentional choices deserve exquisite options."
03

Personality & voice

Personality attributes

  • Confidently sophisticated. Quiet assurance without arrogance
  • Warmly elegant. Gracious and inclusive, never exclusive
  • Thoughtfully innovative. Respects tradition while embracing progress
  • Authentically premium. Quality speaks louder than claims

Communication principles

  • Warmly elegant and gracious. Language feels generous and human, never transactional
  • Polished and precise. Quiet confidence without overselling
  • Cleverly sensory. Elevated language for taste, aroma and texture
  • Direct and transparent. Clear about ingredients and process, with sophisticated honesty

Voice bank

"Everyone deserves something extraordinary in their glass."

"Crafted with purpose. Designed to impress."

"Unexpected pairings. Familiar comforts. Always for the curious."

"Real ingredients. Real process. Real intention."

04

Language rules

Most-referenced section

Always

  • Write BOLLE in all caps
  • Use non-alcoholic, hyphenated
  • Keep the accent on Rosé
  • Write Blanc de Blancs with the second s. It is silent when spoken
  • Spell it Silvaner, never Sylvaner
  • Write ABV as <0.5% ABV or "less than 0.5% ABV"
  • Use US spelling for US content
  • Include neat links to product pages on social posts
  • Use the correct product images and taglines at every touchpoint

Never

  • Say alcohol-free. Non-alcoholic instead
  • Use bright or neon colours in design or graphics
  • Place busy backgrounds or patterns behind the logo or product images
  • Alter the logo's colour or proportions
  • Use the wrong glassware in visuals
  • Use emojis or excessive exclamation marks
  • Use GIFs in stories
  • Use #887711. Retired, see section 05
  • Put #C9AA3A on a light ground, unless it is a recorded exception in section 05

Gold text: the size and ground ladder

Gold as text is governed by 2 things: the ground it sits on, and how big it is. WCAG asks 4.5:1 of text under 24px and 3:1 of text at 24px and above. That gives 3 rungs, and the whole gold family fits them.

GroundSizeUseBarWorst light ground
Ink or ink panelAnyDisplay / dark #C9AA3A3:17.10 on ink panel
Cream or white24px and upDisplay / light #A3892D3:13.26 on cream
Any light groundUnder 24pxGold base #7C5F264.5:15.26 on warm stone
Why is it so hard to make non-alcoholic wine that actually tastes like wine? Display / dark · 7.91:1
Non-alcoholic wine has a science problem Display / light · 3.26:1

The ladder has a floor, not a ceiling

There is no size at which #C9AA3A works on a light ground. Going above 24px lowers the bar from 4.5:1 to 3:1 and stops. It sits at 2.16:1 on cream, under even the relaxed bar, so a bigger heading does not rescue it. That is the whole reason the light rung exists as a separate value.

Always

  • Pick the rung by ground first, then size
  • Keep display gold to an emphasised word or phrase, not a whole heading
  • On warm stone, use gold base at any size. Display / light lands on exactly 3.00 there, which is passing by nothing

Never

  • Put #C9AA3A on a light ground at any size, outside the exceptions recorded below
  • Use either display value in body copy
  • Use them on buttons, chips, borders, rules or icons. They are type colours
  • Use them in print. Neither has a CMYK build

Why these 2 values and not others. #A3892D is the lightest colour at the dark rung's own hue and saturation, 47° and 57%, that clears 3:1 on every light ground we use. It was solved for, not chosen: anything lighter fails. Only lightness moves between the pair, 51% down to 41%, which is why they read as one gold in 2 weights rather than 2 different golds.

This does not un-retire Champagne Gold. #887711 sat at hue 51° and lightness 30% and was a general-purpose accent. Neither display value replaces it, and it stays retired.

The dark band pattern

The dark rung needs a dark ground to sit on, so a page that wants it puts its opening section on ink and returns to the light ground below. Full bleed, cream heading, display gold on the emphasised phrase, body copy at 72% cream. One band per page, at the top. A page with 4 dark bands is a striped page, not a branded one.

Recorded exceptions

The ladder is the rule. Where something live departs from it on purpose, it is written down here rather than left to be discovered. An exception belongs to one named place. It is not a precedent, it does not travel to other pages or channels, and new work follows the ladder.

/pages/how-non-alcoholic-wine-is-made Michelle · 4 Sep 2026
Scope
The 7 display italics at 44.8px on cream, in section bolle-science.Nothing else on the page, and no other page.
Departure
#C9AA3A where the ladder asks for #A3892D
Reason
The light rung was rendered on the page twice and read as brown against a design built around the champagne gold. The hero band keeps #C9AA3A at 7.91:1, and matching the headings to it was judged to matter more here than the ratio.
Cost accepted
2.16:1The emphasised phrase in 7 headings is not legible to low-vision readers. The rest of each heading is, at 17.12:1.
Revisit when
The page is rebuilt, or the design it was matched to changes.

What an exception is not. It is not a licence to use #C9AA3A on light grounds elsewhere. The 4 occurrences on the bolle-best-non-alcoholic-wine section are not covered by the entry above and are still a defect. If that page wants the same treatment, it gets its own decision and its own row, made by looking at it rendered.

Review these when the range or the site changes. An exception made for how one page looks today stops being justified when the page is rebuilt. Anyone reworking a page in this table should re-decide rather than carry the exception across.

Georgia for headlines, Montserrat for everything else. Georgia is a system serif, so it needs no loading and renders reliably everywhere, including email. This guide is set in Georgia and Montserrat only. The system is sufficient.

  • Fallback stacks. Georgia falls back to "Times New Roman", serif. Montserrat falls back to Arial, sans-serif, which is what the site declares and what email needs.
  • Digital weight. Use Montserrat regular for body in digital contexts. Weight, case, line spacing and letter spacing may all be varied for taglines, captions and decorative use.
  • No other faces. Nothing outside Georgia and Montserrat is part of the brand. The single exception is Gelasio, the Canva-only stand-in for Georgia set out below, which is a substitute for one face in one tool rather than a face of its own.

Gelasio, the Canva stand-in

Gelasio, approved 8 September 2026 as the Canva-only stand-in for Georgia. Metric-compatible with Georgia across all 4 styles, licensed SIL OFL.

Why it exists. Georgia is not in the Canva library. Uploading georgia.ttf breaches Microsoft's redistribution terms, and the Monotype desktop licence excludes Canva by name. So Canva work uses Gelasio and everything else uses Georgia.

2 differences that will show

  • Gelasio ships without kerning by design.
  • Its numerals are lining where Georgia's are old-style. Every score, ABV and date will render differently between web and Canva.

Scope. Gelasio is for Canva only. It does not replace Georgia on web, in email, in print or anywhere else, and it is not an alternative anyone may choose between.

The one value
#9D7B3Argb(157, 123, 58). Gold mid, from the scale in section 05.
  • One gold for all 3 marks, on every ground. Type and buttons use 2 golds because the ground is known. A logo file gets reused by people who will not check, so it needs a single value that holds anywhere.
  • Allowed on: hero panels, packaging, merchandise, print, email headers, and decorative or watermark use.
  • Not allowed on: navigation, favicons, small footer marks, or anywhere the mark sits under 40px wide. Use the white or navy master there, because maximum legibility is the point of those.
  • The roundel's inner wordmark is knocked out. Whatever sits behind shows through the letters, so on ink the letters read near-black inside a gold ring. Check the ground before using it.
  • Current gold files are recoloured from the raster master, which is correct for screen, layout and print artwork. Packaging and foil blocking need the vector artwork recoloured at source.

Before a printer quotes a dark substrate

  • The hex is a visual target, not a print spec. CMYK cannot reach a black substrate: process inks are transparent and print onto white. Gold on black needs an opaque spot ink, or an opaque white underbase with gold over it.
  • If the printer offers metallic gold, take it. A real metallic on black beats any flat colour we can specify. Ask for a drawdown on the actual substrate rather than a paper proof.
  • Record the ink he matches to. Add it to this section, so the second run matches the first.
  • Check registration on a white underbase. Misregistration shows as a pale halo around the letters, which is very visible on black.
  • The roundel's inner wordmark is knocked out. On black the letters read as black, correctly. On any other substrate colour they will not.
  • These are raster files. Good to about 135mm wide at 300dpi. Anything larger, or foil or engraving, needs the vector master recoloured at source. That does not exist yet.

Ready made on a ground

  • Two grounds. #111820 is BOLLE Black, the brand's own dark ground, and the one to use unless something says otherwise. #000000 is true black, for merchandise and for surfaces that are already black.

LinkedIn company page

Measured on the live BOLLE Drinks page rather than taken from a spec sheet.

  • LinkedIn crops the company logo to a circle. Anything in the corners of the square is lost, so the mark sits at 82% of the canvas.
  • Use the wordmark, not the roundel. The logo is served at 200px on the page header and renders around 48px next to a post in the feed. At 48px the roundel's inner wordmark closes up and reads as a smudge; the plain wordmark still reads.
  • Upload 400 × 400. Twice what LinkedIn serves on the page, and comfortably over any stated minimum.
  • The cover image is a separate spec. 1128 × 191, and LinkedIn will not hand back anything wider, so upload it at exactly that size. The logo tile covers x 35 to 219 from y 83 down, so nothing legible goes bottom left.

08

Imagery

  • Style: sophisticated, elegant, modern.
  • Setups: minimal, with clean natural lighting. The bottle and the glass are the subject.
  • Glassware matters. Use the correct glass for the wine. The wrong glassware undermines the entire premium claim.
  • No busy backgrounds behind product images, and no pattern competing with the label.
  • No bright or neon colour anywhere in the frame or in graphics laid over it.
09

Audience

PriorityWhoWhat convinces them
P1: Trade Sommeliers, wine directors, owners of premium and luxury on-trade. Michelin-starred restaurants, 5 AA Rosettes, 5-star and 5 AA Red Star hotels, James Beard winners, luxury travel. The wine, tasted blind. Provenance, technique, credibility.
P1: Consumer Sophisticated wine enthusiasts, 30–65+, with developed palates. Moderating for many reasons. Pregnancy, medication, health, driving, early commitments, or simply because they prefer it. Looking and reading like fine wine. Understanding what makes it different.
P2 Mid-premium on-trade: Michelin listed, 3 & 4 AA Rosettes, 4-star hotels, Pinnacle Guide bars, premium travel, luxury catering and events, Nielsen Platinum venues. Luxury off-trade: prestigious premium independents and wine merchants. Category leadership and shelf presence.
P3 Gold on-trade: 1 & 2 AA Rosettes, 3 AA Red Star hotels, Nielsen Gold venues. Mid-premium off-trade: premium chains. Recognition and rate of sale.

Consumer mindsets

  • Discerning quality seekers. Value authenticity and craftsmanship
  • Inclusive hosts. Believe every guest should feel welcomed and celebrated
  • Health-conscious luxury consumers. Want premium experiences without compromise
  • Progressive wine lovers. Open to innovation while respecting tradition
  • Celebration curators. Seek to create meaningful shared moments

The standing tension. Revenue is trade-led, and the trade is convinced by tasting. Consumers cannot taste first, so look and explanation do all the work.

As retail distribution widens, consumer work must avoid discount language, mass-market cues and "now available everywhere". Frame wider availability as wider access to something still exceptional. Premium on-trade accounts are watching.

Reserve tier

Grand Reserve Blanc de Blancs and Chardonnay Reserve are both live. Ultra-premium, lees aged, drawing on multiple varietals from distinguished regions. This is the tier that will need visual differentiation as it grows. See the varietal colour question in section 05.

Proof points

  • Twice fermented, including fermentation after dealcoholisation
  • Lees aged
  • <0.5% ABV
  • 93 points, Wine Enthusiast
  • Poured in 75+ Michelin restaurants
  • Sparkling Rosé, Wine Enthusiast Top 40 Sparkling Wines in the World, 2026

Maintaining this guide

Not yet covered

These do not exist yet. When they are delivered, they belong in this guide as new sections, not as separate files.

  • Textures and patterns. Built from the ring-and-bubbles gesture, with clear-space and opacity rules

  • Explainer diagrams. Twice fermentation, lees ageing, how BOLLE differs from standard dealcoholisation
  • Icon set for the proof points in section 10
  • Social templates and the fill-in guide that goes with them
  • Varietal colour system. Ratifying or replacing the working mapping in section 05

Logos available with the ground already behind them, and a LinkedIn spec.
  • 12 new files in section 07: the 3 marks in gold light and gold pale, each on true black and on BOLLE Black. Transparent masters stay the default; these exist for uploads and third-party templates where the background is out of our hands
  • Gold light carries 2.11:1 on cream and gold pale 1.72:1, so a transparent file flattened to white by an upload form is not a degraded logo, it is an invisible one
  • LinkedIn company page measured rather than looked up: the logo is cropped to a circle, served at 200px and rendered near 48px in the feed, where the roundel's inner wordmark closes up. The wordmark is the mark to use, at 400 × 400
  • The company cover image spec recorded alongside it: 1128 × 191 exactly, because LinkedIn serves no derivative wider than that, and the logo tile occludes x 35 to 219 from y 83 down
v2.8
9 Sep 2026
Gelasio named as the Canva-only stand-in for Georgia.
  • Georgia is not in the Canva library, uploading georgia.ttf breaches Microsoft's redistribution terms, and the Monotype desktop licence excludes Canva by name. Gelasio is metric-compatible across all 4 styles and licensed SIL OFL
  • It is a stand-in, not a second brand typeface. Georgia remains the display face everywhere except Canva, and nobody chooses between them
  • Recorded the 2 visible differences: Gelasio ships without kerning by design, and its numerals are lining where Georgia's are old-style, so every score, ABV and date differs between web and Canva
  • Section 06's "no other faces" rule now names the exception rather than stating an absolute the section itself breaks
  • Footer corrected. It was left reading v2.6 when the cover went to v2.7 on 7 September 2026, so the published guide carried 2 different version numbers

Confidentiality notice added to the cover.
  • The guide is now routinely sent to freelance designers and marketing people before any engagement is signed. The notice tells them what they are holding and what not to do with it
  • Names sections 09, 10 and 11 as the sensitive ones, and says plainly that several BOLLE stockists also sell competing brands
  • Warns against uploading it to third-party tools that train on what they are given

How to update

  • Colour and type changes start on the site. The live storefronts are the source of truth, and this guide follows them.
  • Log every change in the version history above, with the reason. A guide without a changelog stops being trusted.
  • Bump the version on the cover and reissue. Anyone holding an older copy should be able to tell.
  • Owner is responsible for approving changes and for retiring superseded copies.
